q: מטופל בגיר מאושפז זקוק לטיפול רפואי דחוף ואינו מסוגל לתת הסכמה מדעת. אין לו אפוטרופוס, ייפוי כוח תקף או הנחיות מקדימות ידועות. אין בן זוג, ילדים או הורים, ושני אחיו מסכימים מי מהם ייצג אותו. לאחר הליך האישור במוסד, מי מהבאים יכול לשמש מקבל החלטות זמני?
o: הרופא המומחה שקבע את הדחיפות ואת אי־היכולת להסכים
האח הבגיר שנבחר בהסכמה לשמש כנציגו של המטופל
העובד הסוציאלי המרכז את בירור ההסכמה בין קרוביו
מנהל המוסד הרפואי הבוחן את הבקשה לאישור הנציג
explanation:
מקבל החלטות זמני מאפשר להסכים לטיפול דחוף עבור בגיר שאינו מסוגל להסכים. ההליך במוסד מבחין בין בן המשפחה שנבחר לבין אנשי המקצוע המאשרים. **האח הבגיר שנבחר בהסכמה לשמש כנציגו של המטופל**.

**א. הרופא המומחה שקבע את הדחיפות ואת אי־היכולת להסכים.** תפקיד המומחה הוא קביעת הדחיפות והיעדר היכולת להסכים.
**ב. האח הבגיר שנבחר בהסכמה לשמש כנציגו של המטופל.** האח הבגיר יוכל לייצג לאחר השלמת דרישות ההליך והאישור.
**ג. העובד הסוציאלי המרכז את בירור ההסכמה בין קרוביו.** העו״ס בודק את תנאי ההליך ואת הסכמת הקרובים.
**ד. מנהל המוסד הרפואי הבוחן את הבקשה לאישור הנציג.** המנהל או מי שהוסמך לכך בוחן את האישור ואינו הופך לנציג המשפחה.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, מקבל החלטות זמני לעניינים רפואיים, 15.02.2024, עמ׳ 1, 2, סעיפים 1 עד 4ז.

q: A 74-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has urgency incontinence. His family wishes to avoid an antimuscarinic drug. His postvoid residual is 180 mL and blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg. Which listed bladder relaxant acts through beta-3 receptors?
o: Oxybutynin
Mirabegron
Tolterodine
Solifenacin
explanation:
Bladder-storage medicines can relax the detrusor through different receptors. **Mirabegron activates beta-3 receptors**, avoiding antimuscarinic exposure. Residual urine and blood pressure still warrant attention.

**A. Oxybutynin.** Oxybutynin blocks muscarinic receptors and can add cognitive and retention risk.
**B. Mirabegron.** Beta-3 stimulation promotes detrusor relaxation during filling.
**C. Tolterodine.** Tolterodine is an antimuscarinic.
**D. Solifenacin.** Solifenacin also blocks muscarinic signaling and does not satisfy the class requirement.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 712, 714.

q: An 80-year-old woman with moderate vascular dementia in a memory-care unit has refused bathing for two weeks and smells of urine. She becomes aggressive when approached with bathing equipment, but there is no immediate danger. She has hypertension and osteoarthritis and takes amlodipine 5 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg twice daily. Her daughter says she used to be meticulous about cleanliness. Alongside assessing causes of distress, which approach follows first-line behavioral care?
o: Start risperidone before attempting to adjust the bathing routine
Use a sedative before attempting to adjust the bathing routine
Try bathing at a calmer time using a reassuring approach
Increase bedtime medication before attempting to adjust the bathing routine
explanation:
Resistance during bathing may communicate fear, cold, pain or loss of control. **Try a calmer time and a reassuring, individualized approach** after assessing discomfort and the resident's preferences.

**A. Start risperidone before attempting to adjust the bathing routine.** Risperidone before adapting care exposes the patient to avoidable harms.
**B. Use a sedative before attempting to adjust the bathing routine.** A sedative may worsen function and cannot identify what makes bathing distressing.
**C. Try bathing at a calmer time using a reassuring approach.** Offer choice, explain one step at a time and adapt timing or bathing method. These changes target the provoking situation.
**D. Increase bedtime medication before attempting to adjust the bathing routine.** Increasing a bedtime drug does little to address distress provoked specifically by bathing.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 925, 926.
ref: Hazzard Ch 60 — BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS OF DEMENTIA AND PSYCHOACTIVE DRUG THERAPY
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: An 81-year-old woman with dementia taking mirtazapine reports daytime sleepiness. Dose reduction is being considered to reduce sedation. Which information from Hazzard is relevant?
o: Lower doses may increase alertness and reduce daytime sleepiness
Lower doses may remain sedating and leave daytime sleepiness
Lower doses may improve sleep as shown by the described trial
Lower doses may reduce sleepiness as shown by the described trial
explanation:
Mirtazapine can produce daytime sedation through histamine H1 blockade, including at low doses. **Lowering the dose does not guarantee greater alertness.**

**A. Lower doses may increase alertness and reduce daytime sleepiness.** A dose reduction may help an individual, but an increase in alertness cannot be assumed.
**B. Lower doses may remain sedating and leave daytime sleepiness.** Residual sedation can persist at lower doses. Review timing, other sedatives and the indication.
**C. Lower doses may improve sleep as shown by the described trial.** The cited dementia sleep trial does not justify promising better sleep from lower doses.
**D. Lower doses may reduce sleepiness as shown by the described trial.** A reliable reduction in daytime sleepiness was not demonstrated by that trial.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 930.
ref: Hazzard Ch 60 — BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS OF DEMENTIA AND PSYCHOACTIVE DRUG THERAPY
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: An 81-year-old man with severe COPD (FEV1 28% predicted) has been hospitalized three times in six months, lost 20 pounds, and now needs help bathing and dressing. He asks how much time he has left. His daughter interrupts, saying everything will be fine. Which response follows the communication approach described in Hazzard?
o: Acknowledge the difficulty, then provide a fixed survival estimate before exploring preferences
Acknowledge the difficulty, then redirect the discussion to comfort without exploring prognosis
Acknowledge the difficulty, then ask the patient how much prognostic information he wants
Acknowledge the difficulty, then follow the daughter’s preference for avoiding the prognosis
explanation:
Prognostic communication begins by acknowledging emotion and asking what information the patient wants. **Respond to him directly and clarify how much he wants to know**.

**A. Fixed estimate first.** His preferences and prognostic uncertainty should shape the answer.
**B. Redirect to comfort only.** He specifically asked about time and may need it to plan.
**C. Ask his information preference.** Acknowledge his daughter's distress while giving him room to speak.
**D. Follow the daughter's wish.** Her wish to protect him does not determine what he wants to hear.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1090, 1091, 1093.
ref: Hazzard Ch 71 — EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES FOR PATIENTS WITH SERIOUS ILLNESS
chapterTitle: Effective Communication Strategies For Patients with Serious Illness

q: A patient with COPD develops respiratory depression after an opioid overdose. Alongside respiratory support, treatment is needed to reverse the opioid effect. What is the role of naloxone here?
o: Reversal of the opioid effect during an overdose
Long-term medication treatment of opioid use disorder
Enhancement of the opioid effect for pain relief
Replacement of the opioid for continuing pain treatment
explanation:
Naloxone reverses opioid suppression of respiratory drive. COPD limits respiratory reserve, so this patient needs **prompt opioid reversal alongside ventilatory support**.

**A. Reverse the overdose.** By blocking mu-opioid receptors, naloxone can restore spontaneous breathing while assisted ventilation maintains gas exchange.
**B. Treat opioid use disorder long term.** Buprenorphine or methadone can suppress withdrawal and craving over time. Naloxone’s action is brief.
**C. Enhance pain relief.** Opioid receptor blockade can reduce analgesia as it reverses respiratory depression.
**D. Replace the opioid for pain.** Naloxone supplies no analgesia. Reassess the pain regimen once breathing has stabilized.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 326.
ref: Hazzard Ch 23 — SUBSTANCE USE AND DISORDERS

q: במרפאה קרדיולוגית מעוניינים להכניס בדיקה לאבחון שבריריות שתתבצע לפני החלטה על פרוצדורת החלפת מסתם אאורטלי בצינתור Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation (TAVI). מה ההמלצה המתאימה בהתייחס למדדי שבריריות שונים?
o: מדד FRIED ניתן לבצע בתשאול טלפוני
ניתן לבצע מדד Deficit Accumulation Index or Frailty Index (FI) אחרי הערכה כוללנית של גריאטר בקהילה
במידה ורוצים להשתמש באבחון שבריריות מתוך תיק רפואי מומלץ להשתמש במדד Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) של Rockwood
מדד FRAIL מחייב בדיקה גופנית במרפאה
explanation:
The assessment method determines which information must actually be collected. **A Frailty Index can be calculated from deficits documented in a comprehensive geriatric assessment.**

**A. Fried phenotype by telephone** — The original phenotype includes measured handgrip and a timed walk. A telephone interview alone cannot supply those measurements.
**B. Frailty Index after geriatric assessment** — Count eligible deficits present and divide by the number considered. A sufficiently detailed assessment provides the required clinical and functional information.
**C. Use the Clinical Frailty Scale with chart information** — The CFS requires clinical judgment about usual function. A sufficiently informative record can support that judgment, but record-based deficit counting is characteristic of the FI.
**D. FRAIL requires an office examination** — FRAIL asks about fatigue, climbing stairs, walking, illnesses and weight loss. Its items can be elicited by interview.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 621–623, Table 42-3 and Frailty as a Deficit Accumulation.
referenceNote: Printed IMA citation retained; checked explanation source: Hazzard 8e · p. 620-623.

q: A person has low muscle mass, preserved gait/grip, and low food intake without a catabolic disease. Which diagnosis does this chapter prioritize?
o: Malnutrition
Physical frailty
Cachexia
Sarcopenia
explanation:
Low intake can reduce muscle quantity even while strength and gait remain preserved. **In this pattern, prioritize malnutrition and assess the nutritional deficit.**

**A. Malnutrition** Low muscle mass and reduced intake supply the relevant phenotypic and etiologic clues. Clarify the intake history, weight change and other nutritional findings.
**B. Physical frailty** Low mass is not itself a Fried criterion. Preserved grip and gait and the absence of other stated criteria leave physical frailty unsupported here.
**C. Cachexia** Severe wasting from cancer, infection or advanced organ disease would suggest excess catabolism. The history instead points to poor intake.
**D. Sarcopenia** Preserved measured function argues against making sarcopenia the primary diagnosis from low mass alone.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 736, Differential Diagnosis.

q: What core process causes MDS-associated cytopenias?
o: Ineffective clonal hematopoiesis with impaired maturation and differentiation
Destruction of red cells by CLL-associated autoantibodies
A stable diabetic nephropathy satisfying myeloma end-organ criteria
Effective hematopoiesis with unrestricted maturation of affected lineages
explanation:
In MDS, clonal marrow cells fail to mature normally, so blood counts can fall despite a cellular marrow. **Ineffective clonal hematopoiesis with impaired differentiation causes the cytopenias.**

**A. Defective clonal maturation** — Affected precursors fail to produce sufficient functional circulating blood cells.
**B. Autoimmune red-cell destruction** — This can explain hemolytic anemia in CLL. It does not account for dysplastic development of multiple marrow lineages.
**C. Diabetic nephropathy** — Chronic kidney disease can contribute to anemia through reduced erythropoietin. It cannot explain the clonal maturation defect in MDS.
**D. Unrestricted maturation** — Effective differentiation would produce mature blood cells and is the opposite of the marrow process in MDS.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1483–1484.
chapterTitle: Hematologic Malignancies (Leukemia/Lymphoma) and Plasma Cell Disorders
